Common nameAfrican water fern
Other namesCreeping fern or Congo fern
Scientific nameBolbitis heudelotii
DifficultyModerate
LightingLow to moderate
Optimal pH5.0 – 7.0
Optimal GH1 – 6
Optimal temperature71 – 82°F (22 – 28°C)
SubstrateAny (not needed)
Can be grown emersedYes
Growth rateLow
Placement in tankMidground and background
Height10 – 20 inches (25 – 50 cm)
FertilizersLow requirements
CO2Not needed
PropagationThrough rhizome division
ColorDark-green

Note: In scientific literature, Bolbitis species such as B. virens, B. appendiculata and B. presliana are also known as the African water fern.

• Origin: Africa
  • Growth rate: slow
  • Height: 15-30+ cm
  • Light demand: medium
  • CO2: medium
It is presumed that the native habitat of Bolbitis heudelotii is the Congo, from where the plant has spread from Ethiopia in the east to Senegal in the west and down to northern South Africa.

In its natural habitat, this species is generally found attached to driftwood or rocks in streams and relatively fast-flowing rivers, usually in areas with low nutrient levels. These environments are often partly shaded. Example location: Mulembo River.

For the standard plant, use a tank of at least 15 gallons (60 liters) due to its large size.

The mini versions are great for smaller setups, even nano tanks up to 10 gallons (40 liters).

You will need to closely monitor water parameters and avoid fluctuations, including temperature changes:

  • Warm temperature
  • Acidic water
  • Soft water
  • Some current
  • Avoid direct or intense light falling on this plant

This is a slow-growing plant. Even under optimal conditions, the African water fern typically produces only a few new leaves each month.

Do not hesitate to trim away any unhealthy leaves to encourage new growth. The plant tends to grow slightly faster afterward. Do regular water changes.

Sometimes you may see or read that Bolbitis heudelotii grows in regular tap water in some aquariums. However, this can stress it out quickly. Additionally, these tanks often use CO2 and liquid fertilizers. It's not a plant known for great adaptability.

Planting

This is a typical aquatic fern with leaves that grow along its rhizome. Avoid burying the rhizome in the substrate as this can cause decay. Do not plant it directly in the substrate! The roots need free access to oxygen.

Use cotton thread or fishing line to tie this plant to rocks or driftwood. Another option is to use super glue or press it with something heavy (stone, etc.).

To attach the rhizome:

  • clean the surface of the driftwood or rock,
  • apply a drop of glue,
  • attach the fern rhizome,
  • press it firmly.

Approximately 2-3 weeks later, it will strongly attach to any surface, whether smooth or uneven, forming a dense web-like network of roots.

Note: Prevent the fern from drying out by maintaining adequate moisture.

Alternatively, you can simply drop the plant into your tank. Bolbitis heudelotii is heavier than water, so it will naturally sink to the bottom and find its place on its own.

Propagation

In nature, Bolbitis heudelotii propagates by growing little plants (spores) on the underside of the leaf blade (like Java fern does).

In aquariums, it is only propagated through rhizome division. You might notice that the long rhizome appears to 'rot' in the middle or at certain points, and the separated parts go on to live independently.

  • Carefully divide the plant into smaller pieces using a sharp knife, ensuring that each piece has at least 2-3 leaflets.
  • Attach the divided portions to rocks or driftwood.

The plant is sensitive to such propagation and transplanting. It is recommended to divide the rhizome into 2 or at most 3 parts, using only mature and well-established bushes. The stress from separating it from the main rhizome significantly slows down the fern's growth.

When planting, do not cover the rhizome because it will rot, and it is best to plant Bolbitis heudelotii on a root or stone. Keep the plant in position with fishing line until it has gained a hold. Easy to propagate by splitting the horizontal rhizome. Supply of CO2 will considerably enhance the growth, which is only optimal in soft, slightly acidic water.

Temperature: 71 – 82°F (22 – 28°C). This plant does not tolerate cold or too warm water or temperature fluctuations. It stops growing if the temperature drops below 68°F (20°C).

pH: Acidic to neutral (5.0 – 7.0). In alkaline water, leaf dissolution is often observed.

Hardness: Ideally less than 6 GH. In hard water it often melts.

Lighting: In its natural habitat, Bolbitis heudelotii is often found in shaded areas, so this can be replicated in the tank. It's a good fit for low-tech tanks (simple setups without CO2 injection). It thrives in low to medium lighting. Direct sunlight causes burns on the fronds, resulting in brown spots, so it is not recommended to place the tank near a window. The photoperiod should be 8-10 hours per day.

Flow: In some sources it's stated that this plant doesn't require water flow, but the data suggests otherwise. Bolbitis heudelotii prefers clean and fast-flowing water. It degrades in stagnant water pretty quickly.

Substrate: African water fern can grow even in a bare bottom tank, as it can attach itself to the bottom of the aquarium, driftwood, stones, and other objects. The substrate is needed mostly for a more aesthetic look and to enhance conditions for the plant.

CO2 and fertilization: Using a pressurized CO2 system is not mandatory. It will help the ferns grow faster and bushier but, in general, this is completely optional. The plant can survive without fertilizers, but it's still a good idea to use them a few times a month for better growth.

Important: If you plan to add Bolbitis heudelotii to a shrimp tank or a high-tech planted tank (with CO2 and regular fertilization), a high level of CO2 and copper (most fertilizers contain copper) is extremely dangerous to shrimp.

Etymology

The genus name "Bolbitis" is derived from the Greek word "Bolbos", meaning "bulb", referring to the shape of the rhizome or the way the plant attaches itself to surfaces.

The species name "Heudelotii" honours the French botanist and plant collector Jean-Pierre Heudelot (1802–1837), who contributed to the exploration and understanding of plants in Africa during the 19th century.

Taxonomy

Bolbitis heudelotii belongs to a relatively young class, Polypodiopsida. This class encompasses around 10,000 species, with only 120 of them being aquatic ferns.

  • Kingdom: Plantae
  • Division (or Phylum): Pteridophyta
  • Class: Polypodiopsida (Ferns)
  • Order: Polypodiales
  • Family: Dryopteridaceae (Wood fern family)
  • Genus: Bolbitis
  • Species: Bolbitis heudelotii

Description

Bolbitis heudelotii is an aquatic fern characterized by elongated rhizomes and loosely placed leaves.

  • Growth form. Can be grown emersed (in a paludarium) or fully submersed (in aquariums). In nature, it usually grows waterlogged.
  • Size. A relatively large plant, reaching a height of 10 – 20 inches (25 – 50 cm). Excellent for decorating the midground and background.
  • Rhizome. A long and thick (0.4 inches or 1 cm) brown rhizome from which numerous small roots extend. The rhizome is the attachment point for the leaves, referred to as fronds in ferns.
  • Leaves (fronds). The fronds are large and deeply lobed. Technically, fronds are not true leaves but their precursors; what we consider a leaf in Bolbitis is an entire branch, which makes it hard to discern where the leaf blade ends. Young fronds are coiled like a spiral. Fronds grow from the tip rather than the petiole and are arranged alternately. Young and mature fronds differ in appearance: young ones have a more rounded edge, while older ones are serrated or toothed, enhancing the plant's decorative appeal.

The leaves are pretty stiff and durable, covered by a double layer of epidermis. The outer layer, or cortex, has semi-woody cells for protection. The second layer has stomata, allowing the fern to respire. Therefore, in the light, the fronds are adorned with pearly air bubbles.

Note: An interesting characteristic of this fern is the ability of its leaves to orient horizontally, lying attractively on the substrate surface.

  • Color. Dark-green.
  • Roots. African water fern develops a very powerful root system, which allows the plant to anchor to almost any substrate.

Variations

There are two intriguing dwarf morphs of this species:

  • var. Compact: a dwarf variation with a modest height, not exceeding 6 inches (15 cm).
  • var. Baby Leaf: the smallest variation, generally growing up to 3 – 4 inches (7 – 10 cm) in height.

Important: The author has not personally owned the mini versions. Although these types are sold, some aquarists have mentioned that they bought mini versions, but the plants ended up growing into the regular big Bolbitis heudelotii. On the other hand, some people say their mini variations stay small. Perhaps some sellers are not honest, so there is some doubt about what you will get.

Problems

  • Melting: Usually occurs when the plant is transferred from an emersed to a submersed environment or if the water parameters are unstable. Solution: Don't panic. In most cases, the plant will either regrow the leaves or continue growing while developing new submerged leaves. Keep water parameters stable.
  • Turning black or brown: Often attributed to hard and/or alkaline water (>7.0 pH) as well as planting the rhizome too deep in the substrate. Too much iron in the water can also give the fronds a brownish color. Solution: Do not plant it into the substrate. Check your water. Remove all unhealthy leaves so the plant doesn't waste energy on them.
  • Growth rate: It can take a long time to adapt and grow in a new environment. Solution: This is a very slow-growing plant, so do not expect much from it.
  • Ugly shape: Appearance suffers if old growth is not trimmed regularly. Solution: Trim the plant and remove old leaves.
  • Algae: Like other slow-growing aquarium plants, it is highly susceptible to algae and may die because of it. Solution: Adjust the lighting intensity, do regular water changes, and introduce algae-eaters. You can also clean the plant with a soft brush.
  • Overgrowth: Bolbitis heudelotii is a large plant and can shade its neighbors, blocking light from reaching plants at the bottom of the tank. Solution: Prune and discard the dense mass from time to time to prevent overcrowding and shading at the surface.
  • Relocation: Bolbitis does not tolerate disturbance; even moving it can lead to a prolonged period of distress. Solution: Be extra careful with this plant.

Benefits

  • Aquascape: This plant can grow not only vertically but also horizontally, gracefully resting on driftwood, rocks and other elements. The popularity of aquatic ferns rose after Takashi Amano incorporated them into his tropical compositions.
  • Foraging place: The structure of the plant acts like a buffet of biofilm and catches free-floating particles, creating a natural feeding ground for shrimp, which will constantly graze on it.
  • Hard structure: The relatively rigid leaves and structure make it a good choice for aquariums where fish may nibble on plants (such as goldfish), within reasonable limits.
  • Oxygenation: Helps generate oxygen in the tank water. It produces small pearls or bubbles of oxygen that stay on top of the plant, adding a very lively aspect.

Quarantine

Unless you are completely sure that Bolbitis heudelotii is safe, for example it was grown in sterile/laboratory conditions (in vitro) and the in vitro pot is not damaged or opened, quarantine and disinfect it first to avoid the risk of contamination and poisoning. Do not introduce a new plant to your tank right after buying it.

  • The plant can carry parasites, pests like snails, or even predators (dragonfly, damselfly nymphs, etc.).
  • It may contain residues of chemicals (pesticides) used to remove parasites, snails, etc. These chemicals are extremely poisonous to fish, shrimp and other invertebrates.

Conclusion

Bolbitis heudelotii is an attractive and decorative aquarium plant. Its unique dark-green leaves and versatility in aquascaping make it popular among aquarium enthusiasts. It is an excellent choice for creating a tropical atmosphere in the aquarium. Although it is not for beginners, it is relatively easy to grow when its specific requirements are met. Proper lighting, suitable temperature and water parameters will ensure its healthy growth and beauty.
Bolbitis comes from West Africa, a fern with beautiful, transparent green leaves, 15-40 cm tall and wide.
